title: Keeping the counter straight on a busy day
target: How the money at a counter in TCG Card Shop Simulator actually works: pieces of cash are objects with a value and an index, the counter holds the currency list, and a customer's payment can be scanned, boxed and moved like anything else.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with a counter and a register
A moment to look at what is on the counter

steps.do: Treat what is on the counter as objects rather than as a running total, because each piece knows what it is.
steps.because: a piece of money at the counter can be a coin or a note and carries that on the object (InteractableCounterMoneyChange, m_CanBeCoinOrBill, m_IsCoin)

steps.do: Read the value from the piece itself when something looks wrong, because the value is kept on the object in two forms plus an index.
steps.because: each piece carries an ordinary value, a more precise one and an index (m_Value, m_ValueDouble, m_Index)

steps.do: Remember that the counter owns the list of currencies, so a piece means nothing without it.
steps.because: the counter keeps a list of currency data that the money refers to (m_CounterMoneyChangeCurrencyDataList, CounterMoneyChangeCurrencyData)

steps.do: Take the customer's payment as an object too, because cash and a card are two different things with a model each.
steps.because: the payment knows whether it is a card and has a cash model and a card model (InteractableCustomerCash, m_IsCard, m_CashModel, m_CardModel)

steps.do: Scan a payment rather than working it out by eye, because scanning at the counter is something the payment allows.
steps.because: a payment can be scanned at the counter (m_CanScanByCounter)

steps.do: Clear up by boxing and moving money like any other object, keeping to the shop and warehouse rules.
steps.because: money can be boxed and moved, and it carries rules for being placed in the shop or the warehouse (m_CanBoxUpObject, m_PlaceObjectInShopOnly, m_PlaceObjectInWarehouseOnly)

steps.do: Set the counter up through its own screens instead of treating it as fixed, because the register and its settings are things of their own.
steps.because: the counter has a register and a setting screen of its own (CashRegister, SetCashierCounterSettingScreen)

steps.do: Expect a currency to be a set of pictures rather than a recolour, because each one has its own sheet of coins and notes.
steps.because: the game ships a texture sheet for each currency with both coins and notes on it (T_MoneyCoinEuro, T_MoneyCoinYen)

commonMistakes: Treating the pile on the counter as a number and never checking what is actually there.
Assuming a card and cash behave the same way, when each has its own model and outline.
Eyeballing a payment instead of scanning it at the counter.
Leaving money loose when it can be boxed and moved like any other object.
Expecting a new currency to look like the old one recoloured, when each ships its own sheet.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
